\section{World and Element Notation Audit}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5!white,colframe=green!65!black,title=\textbf{Consistent Usage Confirmed}]
The following world and element notation is used consistently across all documents.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection{World Symbols (Consistent)}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{c|c|l}
\toprule
\textbf{World} & \textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Status} \\
\midrule
Archetypal & $A$ & Consistent \\
Intellectual/Mental & $B$ & Consistent \\
Conceptual/Emotional & $C$ & Consistent (note: naming varies) \\
Material/Physical & $D$ & Consistent \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{Minor Issue}: World B is called ``Intellectual'' in v7.4 but ``Mental'' in scenario docs. World C is called ``Conceptual'' in v7.4 but ``Emotional'' in scenario docs.

\textbf{Recommendation}: Add alternative names in v7.4 glossary: ``B (Intellectual/Mental)'' and ``C (Conceptual/Emotional/Formative)''.

\subsection{Element Notation (Consistent)}
The element notation $Wn^k_{mf}$ is used consistently:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $W \in \{A, B, C, D\}$: World
    \item $n \in \{1, \ldots, 10\}$: Mode within world
    \item $k \in \{0, \ldots, 9\}$: Noetic operator superscript
    \item $mf \in \{1a, \ldots, 7d\}$: Sub-foundation subscript
\end{itemize}

\section{Recommendations Summary}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!5!white,colframe=yellow!75!black,title=\textbf{Priority 1: Resolve Conflicts (BEFORE v7.5)}]
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Rename \verb|\Hyperstition| from $\mathcal{H}$ to $\mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{hyp}}$ to avoid conflict with $\mathcal{H}$ (Hilbert space)
    \item Rename \verb|\Collapse| from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ to avoid conflict with $\mathcal{C}$ (QuantumChannel)
    \item Disambiguate vulnerability ($\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{vuln}}$) from virality ($\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{viral}}$)
\end{enumerate}
\end{tcolorbox}
